name: Google Glass Enterprise Edition 2
summary: Google Glass Enterprise Edition 2 was a head-worn display sold to businesses for hands-free work, offered from 2019 and withdrawn by Google in 2023.
description: Google Glass Enterprise Edition 2, model GG2; enterprise assisted-reality wearable. Excludes Explorer Edition and Enterprise Edition 1.
tier_reason: A particular enterprise product and withdrawal case is fine detail; do not give it the consequence of wearable displays as a class. This is a scoped consequence judgement, not a reward for documentation or representation.

market.note: The product was commercially offered through enterprise solution partners.

evidence.supports: Invites businesses to contact sales or solution partners starting that day.
Reports EE2 available for business through third-party partners with MSRP $999.

date.label: 8 August 2018
date.basis: SGS report records the sample received on this date.

events.statement: The test laboratory received a Glass Enterprise Edition 2 GG2 sample.
events.scope: Google Glass Enterprise Edition 2, GG2 test sample
events.caveats: The report does not call this sample a prototype or specify when the model was invented or first built.

evidence.supports: Test lab received a sample identified as EE2, model GG2, on 8 August 2018.

date.label: May 2019
date.basis: Google dates launch to May; 20 May begins contact with sales/partners and a 21 May trade report says partner availability.

events.statement: Google announced Glass Enterprise Edition 2 on 20 May 2019 and invited enterprise customers to contact its sales team or partners; a 21 May report described partner availability.
events.scope: Glass Enterprise Edition 2 partner offer reported in May 2019; first commercial-offer date not established.
events.caveats: Google invited sales inquiries on 20 May; the independent availability report is dated 21 May. These do not establish the first transaction or exclude earlier private arrangements.

evidence.supports: Invites businesses to contact sales or solution partners starting that day.
Reports EE2 available for business through third-party partners with MSRP $999.
Dates launch to previous May and describes a new direct reseller channel for developers.

date.label: 4 February 2020
date.basis: Google announced direct reseller purchasing for developers on this day.

events.statement: On 4 February 2020 Google said developers and businesses could purchase Glass Enterprise Edition 2 devices directly from named hardware resellers.
events.scope: Google Glass Enterprise Edition 2: dated direct-reseller offer; purchase quantities and first offer date unknown.
events.market: Developers and businesses using named hardware resellers; order quantity unspecified.
events.caveats: Channel expansion, not the initial commercial introduction.

evidence.supports: Dates launch to previous May and describes a new direct reseller channel for developers.

date.label: By 15 March 2023
date.basis: Google says that as of 15 March it would no longer sell the family. This establishes a latest cessation date, not the exact first day without sales.

events.statement: By 15 March 2023 Google was no longer selling Glass Enterprise Edition, including Edition 2; reseller withdrawal and last actual device use are not established.
events.scope: Google vendor sales of Glass Enterprise Edition 2
events.caveats: No claim about last reseller sale, production, or actual installed-device use. Google says devices and existing software could continue after the support cutoff.

evidence.supports: By 15 March 2023 Google said it no longer sold Glass Enterprise Edition; support ends 15 September 2023; existing software/devices may continue to work.

evidence.locator: Edition 2 product heading and sales notice
evidence.supports: Places the family-level Google withdrawal notice in the Edition 2 help context.

date.label: 15 September 2023
date.basis: Google states support/replacement under the described process continues until this date.

events.statement: Google identified a support and replacement cutoff for Glass Enterprise Edition.
events.scope: Google support and replacement process for Glass Enterprise Edition
events.caveats: A support cutoff is not a proven universal device end-of-use. Meet support may end while local device software remains usable.

evidence.supports: By 15 March 2023 Google said it no longer sold Glass Enterprise Edition; support ends 15 September 2023; existing software/devices may continue to work.

evidence.locator: Edition 2 product heading and sales notice
evidence.supports: Places the family-level Google withdrawal notice in the Edition 2 help context.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest defensible dated record of this scoped referent in the retained evidence; later community entry is recorded separately. SGS report records the sample received on this date. The report does not call this sample a prototype or specify when the model was invented or first built. This is the earliest supported record currently established here, not certification of absolute priority.

community_entry.community: Enterprise customers purchasing through Google’s sales or partner channel
community_entry.rationale: The May 2019 enterprise-channel offer and 21 May partner-availability report support availability by that time; direct developer resellers came later in 2020.
community_entry.caveats: The event is month-precision and does not prove first transaction, availability in every market, or direct reseller purchase in May 2019.

caveats: A May 2019 enterprise partner offer and a February 2020 direct-reseller offer are documented. Purchase quantities and the dates of first offers are unknown; prior private arrangements were not excluded.

unresolved.note: GG2 sample was tested before launch; its invention and prototype dates were not established.

evidence.supports: Test lab received a sample identified as EE2, model GG2, on 8 August 2018.

unresolved.note: May 2019 sources establish a launch and partner offer, not when the first offer began or whether earlier private commercial arrangements existed.

evidence.supports: Invites businesses to contact sales or solution partners starting that day.
Reports EE2 available for business through third-party partners with MSRP $999.
Dates launch to previous May and describes a new direct reseller channel for developers.

unresolved.note: Google expressly says devices and existing software could still be used after support ended; no date of last actual use or verified 2026 use was located.
